001: Ivan, hi! Have you seen my history notebook? I think I left it in the classroom.
Hi, Anna. No, I haven't seen it. Did you definitely take it to the last class?
Yes, I definitely took it. Maybe I left it on the table by the window.
I'll go check right now. And if I don't find it, I'll ask the class monitor.
Thank you so much, you'd really be saving me.
Don't mention it. Wait here for me for a couple of minutes.
002: Dmitry, have you had lunch yet? Olga and I are going to the cafeteria, do you want to come with us?
I'd love to, but I'm finishing the sandwich I brought from home.
That's too bad, they're serving a really tasty soup there today.
Really? Okay, you've convinced me. I'll go with you, and I'll save the sandwich for later.
Great. Then get ready, we'll wait for you by the entrance.
Alright, I'll just grab my jacket and head out right away.
003: Sergey, do you know when our next philosophy lecture is?
I think it's on Thursday at ten in the morning. Why, have they already assigned something?
Yes, the professor asked us to read two chapters from the textbook.
I see. Have you read it already? Maybe you could share your notes?
I only managed to get through the first chapter, it's pretty difficult.
Then we can go over the second one together on Wednesday evening at the library.
004: Olga, you look tired. Is everything okay?
Yeah, I was just up late last night working on my psychology paper.
I didn't even know we were assigned such a big paper.
It was only assigned to my group. But I'm almost done, there's just a little left.
Good for you! If you need any help with the formatting, just ask.
Thanks, Anna. I'll definitely keep your offer in mind.
005: Alexey, hi! Are you going to English class?
Hi, Maria. I am, but honestly, I didn't get any sleep at all.
Were you playing video games until late again?
Yeah, I got a bit carried away with the guys in an online tournament.
Wow, you're something else. How are you going to answer in class then?
I'll try not to embarrass myself. I'll grab a coffee now, that should help.
006: Ivan, do you know where I can print documents on the second floor?
I do, there's a special machine right next to the dean's office.
Is it working? I heard it breaks down sometimes.
It was working yesterday, I printed my notes there myself. Come on, I'll show you.
That would be great, because I need to submit an application urgently.
Then let's not waste any time, let's go right now.
007: Dmitry, have you chosen a topic for your term paper yet?
Not yet, I just can't make up my mind. I have a couple of ideas, but they're rough.
What are you thinking about? Maybe I can help somehow.
I'm interested in the topic of the economic crisis, but it's too broad.
Maybe you should narrow it down to a specific country or time period?
That's a good idea. Thanks for the advice, I'll think it over.
008: Elena, hi! Have you seen my blue backpack? I left it in the classroom yesterday.
Hi, Anna. I haven't seen it. Did you check the coat check?
I did, it's not there. I've been looking everywhere for it.
Maybe you left it in the cafeteria? You did go there yesterday.
That's right! I completely forgot that I went there after classes.
Then go quickly, before someone takes it.
009: Sergey, do you want to go to a contemporary art exhibition on Saturday?
Where is it being held? I haven't heard anything about it.
At the city museum, there will be several halls with new works.
Sounds interesting. What time are you planning to go?
Let's go at two in the afternoon, so we don't have to rush.
It's a deal. Then we'll meet at the museum entrance on Saturday.
010: Olga, have you gotten your math test results yet?
Not yet, but the professor said he'll announce them at the end of the week.
I'm really worried that I failed. The last problem was difficult.
Don't worry so much, you studied for it. I'm sure you passed.
Thanks for the support. How do you think you did yourself?
Okay, but not without mistakes either. We'll just wait and hope.
